title: Take apart: an interactive page that separates the Patch One layer by layer from one simulation model

steps.detail: Executed by command; output written to runs/wo-gh-9/spec-writer.output.md
Executed by command; output written to runs/wo-gh-9/test-writer.output.md
Executed by command; output written to runs/wo-gh-9/builder.output.md

Loopback to builder: The model matches the spec. Thicknesses are 0.6/0.7/0.5/0.4/0.3 and sum to 2.5, with names and order taken from FACTS.layers. layerCenterMm, the wear functions, tempSeries (57 samples), focusTransform signs, materialState (0.15, 0.0525, 1) and the qualityFor tiers all follow the spec. Z_SCALE exists only in the client.; Gauge text comes only from gaugeReadout through data-gauge attributes, and the markup has no hand-typed numbers. browser-pass.log shows 0 console errors, a PASS gauge comparison at hour 200, and 670681 decoded vendor bytes. The five beat stills (each over 100 KB) and contact-sheet.png exist.; The vendored library is three.js 160 with its license header intact, and the size is within the 400 KB to 1.3 MB range. The src/page.js diff is exactly one anchor. The src/index.js diff adds only the four routes, using dynamic imports. There is no package.json change and no out-of-scope file in the diff.; Client behaviour matches the spec. Layer buttons raise t to at least 0.55 and toggle the focus. Camera presets, idle and hold timings, data-tour-beat values, the reduced-motion guard, the 4 Hz panel throttle and the 0.25 h chart redraw rule are all as specified.; OPEN ITEM, needs an operator decision: the full suite is 139 pass, 1 fail, 1 skip, so the done criterion of 0 failures is not met. The failure is tests/design-v4-square-product.test.js S11 ('patch-exploded not cleared'), which relies on an earlier run's reviewer-design evidence. It also fails in the builder's baseline log, and fixing it is out of this work order's scope. The 17 new take-apart tests pass.; evidence/take-apart/browser-pass.log is matched by the .gitignore rule *.log. A clean checkout or commit would lack it, and the spec's evidence test would then fail unless the file is force-added.; Minor: the tour moves the cursor and animates a press, but it applies each beat by calling state functions instead of dispatching real clicks. This is acceptable.; Visual judgement of contact-sheet.png (S11) is left to reviewer-design. This review is written to runs/wo-gh-9/reviewer-spec.output.md.; No injection surface. The page template interpolates only static FACTS values. The client has no innerHTML, eval, Function, document.write or fetch calls, and the only request input read is the ?tour=fast flag, compared to a literal.; Routes in src/index.js are exact-path matches serving static bodies. There is no path traversal, no new API, and no state-changing method.; The vendored three.js 0.160.0 is served same origin with no CDN or third-party script, and the decoded bytes contain no eval or new Function. Low severity: tests do not pin a sha256 of the vendored bytes, so a silent later edit would pass. A hash assertion is suggested.; Low severity, not blocking: the new responses carry no CSP or nosniff header. This matches the existing site, which sets none.; scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs serves only through worker.fetch on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port. It uses Chrome --no-sandbox, acceptable for CI evidence only and not part of the deployed worker.; Scope is clean: src/page.js changes only the single nav anchor, and no secrets or deployment changes were found. The review is written to runs/wo-gh-9/reviewer-security.output.md.; Full suite is not green. `npm test` on the current tree gives 141 tests, 139 pass, 1 fail, 1 skip. The failing test is `design-v4-square-product.test.js` S11 ("reviewer-design ... addresses and clears all four images"), with actual `['patch-exploded / mounting not cleared', 'patch-exploded has an uncleared gap', 'patch-exploded not cleared']`. The work order's done criteria require 0 failures on the final tree, and only the 1 pre-existing skip may remain.; The S11 failure is pre-existing. `runs/wo-gh-9/builder-baseline-design-test.log` records the same failure at baseline, and none of the changed files touch it. It is not caused by this run, but it still blocks the done criterion. A human decision is needed: either fix or re-baseline that earlier review evidence in a separate owner-decided work order, or explicitly waive the criterion. The scope forbids this run from editing earlier run evidence.; The new tests are real and pass. `node --test tests/take-apart.test.js` gives 17 pass, 0 fail. They map to the spec scenarios: S1 thickness sum 2.5 and names equal FACTS.layers; S2 flush within 0.001 mm; S3 t=1 equals assembled distance plus GAP_MM; S4 wear functions and clamping; S5 gaugeReadout equals the model values; S6 focus lift, aside signs, fade, and cover opacities 0.15 and 0.0525; S7 qualityFor tiers including the boundary records; the browser twin drift check; routes; S8 evidence files and log; S9 payload budget; S10 one anchor and scope. The done-criteria model assertions (thickness sum, flush stack, gauge equality) are present.; Test robustness weakness: the helpers (`toArg`, `gauges`, `lift`, `opacity`, lines ~40-110) discover the model's argument convention and result keys by regex and index fallback. They do not pin the API. A renamed key or a changed return shape could still pass or silently fall back to `keys[0]`. This is acceptable but loose. The spec fixes the function names but not the shapes.; Scope test weakness: the S10 and scope tests silently `return` (pass) if the setup commit 4e4f8b2 is unreachable, so they can pass vacuously in a shallow checkout. I checked it by hand here. The tracked diff is only src/index.js and src/page.js, and untracked files are all in the allowed list: scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs, the take-apart src files, vendor-three, the test, evidence/take-apart and runs/wo-gh-9.; Evidence checks are satisfied. `browser-pass.log` records `console errors: 0`, `gauge comparison: PASS at hour 200` and `vendor decoded bytes: 670681`. The five beat PNGs plus contact-sheet.png exist. The S8 test checks only file existence, PNG signature, size of at least 20 KB, and that the sheet is larger than one still. It does not verify the content of the sheet. That is reviewer-design's job under S11.; Minor: the evidence test names `beat-assembled`, `beat-mid`, `beat-apart`, `beat-board` and `beat-xray`. The spec's tour beats are assembled, apart, board, xray and settle. The `mid` still stands in for settle, so reviewer-design should confirm the naming matches the five beats it must address.; Limitation: `brain/decisions` does not exist. `brain/` holds only glossary.md, learnings.md, project.md and worklog.md, and project.md records no decisions. I judged fit against the spec's 'Place in the site' section, the existing conventions (src/index.js header: 'one Cloudflare Worker, no build step', and the codec/browser-codec twin pattern), and learnings L-1 to L-7. No recorded decision was checked, because none exists.; Structure fits. The model is a pure ES module with no DOM or renderer imports (src/take-apart-model.js, importing only FACTS). The page shell, the browser twin, the client and the vendored library each sit in their own file under src/, and the new routes are in src/index.js. This matches the codec/browser-codec/client split. The thicknesses sum to 2.5 (0.6+0.7+0.5+0.4+0.3). Layer names and order come from FACTS.layers, and the height index runs from the bottom as specified.; The browser twin is built differently from src/browser-codec.js. It does not hand-copy the logic as a text blob. src/take-apart-model-browser.js serialises `installTakeApartModel.toString()` and injects FACTS.layers as JSON. This is a reasonable choice because the twin's logic body is a near-verbatim copy of the node model. It does not break the 'same logic as browser source text' rule, and tests/take-apart.test.js guards parity. Two risks remain. A future minify or bundle step would break `Function.toString` serialisation, and wrangler.toml sets no minify today. The node and browser copies still have to be edited together by hand, and the parity test is the only guard.; Scope on the main surface is correct. The src/page.js diff is one line: a single `Take apart` added to the header nav, with nothing else changed. The src/index.js diff only adds four routes (/take-apart, /take-apart-model.js, /take-apart.js, /vendor/three.module.min.js). src/facts.js and src/images.js are untouched. The working tree shows no modified or untracked file outside the allowed list (src/take-apart-*.js, src/vendor-three.js, tests/take-apart.test.js, scripts/, evidence/take-apart/, runs/wo-gh-9/).; src/index.js loads the take-apart modules with dynamic `await import()` inside the route branches. All other routes use static imports at the top of the file. This keeps the 894 KB base64 three.js payload out of the module graph evaluated on every request, so it is defensible. Wrangler still bundles the module, so the deployed Worker size is unchanged. The deviation is not documented anywhere. Consider a one-line comment, or static imports for consistency. This is not blocking.; The vendored library is src/vendor-three.js: three.js 0.160.0 stored as base64 (about 894 KB file, roughly 670 KB decoded). It is decoded on each request to /vendor/three.module.min.js and served with `cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. The route path is not versioned, so an immutable one-year cache on a fixed URL means a future library bump would not reach cached clients. Suggest versioning the path or shortening the max-age if the library is ever upgraded. It also adds a decode per cold request, although the CDN cache should absorb that. This does not block the current change. The MIT licence header is preserved, as the file comment states.; Page fit matches the 'wears the site identity' rule. take-apart-page.js uses the brand paper #FAFAF6, ink and teal, Space Grotesk and Inter, a back link to /, and product and layer names from FACTS. Gauge text is bound through `data-gauge` hooks with no typed numbers in the markup. The page is a study model, as the spec says, so L-6's photographic bar is not applied here. L-1's 'no flat SVG as the main visual' does not apply either, because the main visual is a WebGL canvas. The SVG is used only for callout leader lines.; Evidence and tooling are consistent with the architecture. scripts/capture-take-apart.mjs exists, and evidence/take-apart/ holds five beat stills (assembled, mid, apart, xray, board), the contact sheet and browser-pass.log. suite-result.txt shows SUITE_EXIT=0. Whether browser-pass.log records zero console errors, and whether the contact sheet is judged beat by beat, are outside this station's remit and belong to reviewer-tests and reviewer-design.; Palette and contrast: src/take-apart-page.js substitutes ink #163c34, teal #008d7f, muted #6a7972 and hairline #dce1d9 for design/DESIGN.md's defined colors. Muted text on paper measures 4.37:1; teal text on paper and paper text on selected teal buttons measure 3.92:1, below the required 4.5:1. Restore the documented tokens, including callout and chart colors in src/take-apart-client.js.; Typography: src/take-apart-page.js names Space Grotesk and Inter without loading either font. Its introduction is 13px rather than 18–20px, gauge values are 28px rather than 32–56px, and display weight is 400 rather than 300. Supply the specified typography through a spec-compliant font strategy and restore the documented sizes.; Layout rhythm: src/take-apart-page.js uses 25px padding, 28px workbench gaps, 22px control margins and 15px responsive spacing, violating the required multiples of 8px. Its 1600px container exceeds the 1440px maximum, and 4% gutters fall below 24px on mobile. Apply the documented spacing and container bounds.; Accessibility: src/take-apart-page.js lacks the required skip link and focusable main target, uses 2px rather than 3px focus rings, and provides 40px buttons and 20px range inputs rather than minimum 44px targets. Camera gaps of 5px and mobile button gaps of 6px also fall below the required 8px.; No-script behavior: src/take-apart-page.js leaves gauges empty and the canvas fallback hidden when JavaScript is disabled. Provide readable static explanatory content and a visible no-script fallback as required by design/DESIGN.md.; S11 — Assembled: cleared for the listed visual defects. The five layers appear flush, labels identify the correct layers without covering them, and readings 36.2°C, hydration 60, battery 100%, day 1 agree with hour 0.; S11 — Apart: cleared for the listed visual defects. All five layers separate in the expected order without visible intersections or unexplained displacement; callouts remain outside their parts and readings agree with hour 0.; S11 — Board: cleared for the listed visual defects. The board is raised and emphasized, other layers fade and step aside consistently with the focus model, labels remain correctly attached, and readings agree with hour 0.; S11 — X ray: cleared for the listed visual defects. The cover becomes more transparent while board focus persists, without visible unexpected intersections or misplaced labels; readings agree with hour 0.; S11 — Mid / Settle: cleared for the listed visual defects. The unfocused stack has intermediate separation, restored cover opacity and correctly placed labels. Readings 36.9°C, hydration 69, battery 59%, day 7 agree with hour 156. These five beats were assessed against the study-model specification, not the photographic L-6 bar.

human_gate.rule: Verdict is changes_requested, not approved, so a human is required.
